description: This bar chart illustrates the correlation between different population metrics and content categories. The horizontal axis displays the categories “Movies,” “Songs,” and “Basketball,” listed alphabetically. The vertical axis, labeled “Correlation,” presents a linear scale ranging from 0 to 0.7, with tick marks at 0.1 intervals. Four bars are present for each category, representing “Pop<sub>GT</sub>” in a light orange color, “Pop<sub>GE</sub>” in a medium orange color, “RPop<sub>GT</sub>” in a light blue color, and “RPop<sub>GE</sub>” in a dark blue color, as indicated by the legend. For the “Movies” category, the “Pop<sub>GT</sub>” bar reaches approximately 0.2, “Pop<sub>GE</sub>” reaches approximately 0.3, “RPop<sub>GT</sub>” reaches approximately 0.6, and “RPop<sub>GE</sub>” reaches approximately 0.65. In the “Songs” category, the “Pop<sub>GT</sub>” bar reaches approximately 0.3, “Pop<sub>GE</sub>” reaches approximately 0.5, “RPop<sub>GT</sub>” reaches approximately 0.55, and “RPop<sub>GE</sub>” reaches approximately 0.6. For “Basketball,” the “Pop<sub>GT</sub>” bar reaches approximately 0.05, “Pop<sub>GE</sub>” reaches approximately 0.1, “RPop<sub>GT</sub>” reaches approximately 0.15, and “RPop<sub>GE</sub>” reaches approximately 0.2. The bars are grouped by category, with each group containing the four population metrics stacked side-by-side. No bars are visually emphasized through shading, bolding, outlining, or annotation.
